research.abstract: Insect chemosensory receptors are essential for detecting environmental chemical cues that influence insect survival and behavior. Advances in genome and transcriptome sequencing have expanded the identification of olfactory receptors (ORs), gustatory receptors (GRs), and ionotropic receptors (IRs), while also providing new opportunities to investigate their expression, evolution, and function. Nevertheless, the functions of many identified receptors remain unknown. This review summarizes recent methods and findings in insect chemosensory receptor research, covering receptor identification and annotation using genomic and transcriptomic data, cell-specific expression analysis using single-cell and single-nucleus sequencing, and evolutionary analysis based on comparative genomics and phylogenetics. We also discuss structural studies of OR-Orco complexes and GRs, computational approaches to receptor-ligand prediction, including structure modeling, molecular docking, and machine learning, and experimental methods for functional characterization. Finally, we discuss how multi-omics integration can combine complementary data layers, such as transcriptomic and chromatin-accessibility data, to improve the identification and interpretation of insect chemosensory receptors. By examining how these approaches complement one another, we highlight current progress and outstanding challenges in linking receptor sequences to ligand recognition and biological function.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Tuberculosis Diagnosis delays among tuberculosis patients can worsen infection transmission, disease severity, and mortality risk. Identifying factors influencing delays is crucial due to its persistence across healthcare levels and communities. The study identify determinants of tuberculosis diagnosis delay among patients attending public health facility of Metekel zone, Northwest Ethiopia:2023 Methods An unmatched case-control study was conducted in Metekel zone health facilities from March to April 2023, involving 210 tuberculosis patients (103 cases, 107 controls) selected through systematic sampling. Data collected through structured questionnaires and STATA used for analysis, including bi-variable and multi-variable logistic regressions. Variables with p-value < 0.25 in bi-variable analysis were included in the final model after checking model fitness and multicollinearity. Results Overall, 210 tuberculosis patients were included in the study. The following independent variables were associated diagnosis delay of tuberculosis: TB patients who travel greater than 10km (AOR: 2.941, (95 % CI: 1.509, 5.731); TB patients who are living at rural area (AOR: 4.135, 95 % CI :1.759, 9.723); TB patients who prior visit in holly-water and traditional medicine [AOR: 2.978, (95% CI: 1.292, 6.863); poor knowledge about TB [AOR: 2.826, (95% CI: 1.404, 5.687)]. Conclusion Tuberculosis diagnosis delay is a major challenge to eliminate tuberculosis by breaking the chain of transmission. This study can be attributed to factors including place of residence being rural, poor knowledge about tuberculosis, non-health facility initial actions upon symptom onset, and far distance to health institutions. Recognizing these determinants helps in identifying and addressing barriers inhibiting early diagnosis, potentially improving healthcare access and promoting more timely diagnosis and treatment for tuberculosis patients.

research.abstract: Abstract Local adaptation is contingent on genotype-by-environment interactions, which are often mediated by variation in gene expression. The causes and consequences of variation in gene expression are complex, and they are rarely evaluated under the multi-dimensional environmental regimes that occur in the field. Here, we investigate switchgrass gene expression variation in contrasting sites in Michigan and Texas. We examined differentially expressed genes between upland and lowland switchgrass genotypes and found that genes with genotype x environment (GxE) interactions were enriched for GO terms related to phosphorus metabolism. After mapping expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) in a switchgrass diversity panel in both sites, we compared distinct categories of eQTL to investigate their effects on gene expression in contrasting environments and their evolutionary history. Cis regulatory variants are more likely to have consistent effects across sites, while trans regulatory variants were more likely to have site-specific effects, and are more likely to underlie changes in gene expression between sites. Lower minor allele frequency in trans regulatory variants is consistent with stronger purifying selection. Furthermore, site-specific regulatory variants exhibited intermediate minor allele frequencies, consistent with balancing selection or soft sweeps. Finally, motivated by enrichment for phosphorus-related genes exhibiting differential expression between sites, we conducted a GWAS for leaf phosphorus concentration in the diversity panel. By overlaying the GWAS results with the eQTL map, we characterized cis and trans regulation of candidate genes for leaf P concentration in Michigan and Texas. Together, this work provides novel insights on the molecular basis and evolutionary history of GxE interactions in switchgrass.

research.abstract: Importance: Standard repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation protocols are difficult to integrate into inpatient psychiatric care because they require daily treatment over several weeks. Accelerated intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) may offer a feasible augmentation strategy for hospitalized patients with treatment-resistant depression (TRD). Objective: To determine whether connectivity-guided accelerated iTBS improves depressive symptoms beyond routine multimodal inpatient care in hospitalized patients with TRD. Design, Setting, and Participants: This randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled clinical trial was conducted in the inpatient unit of the Department of Psychiatry, University of Oldenburg, Karl-Jaspers-Klinik, Bad Zwischenahn, Germany. Patients aged 18 to 65 years with unipolar TRD were recruited between May 2021 and August 2024. Interventions: Participants received active or sham iTBS targeting an individualized left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex site showing strongest functional anticorrelation with the subgenual anterior cingulate cortex using resting-state functional MRI. Treatment was delivered as 3 daily sessions over 10 weekdays (30 sessions; 54 000 pulses total) as augmentation to routine multimodal inpatient care. Main Outcomes and Measures: Primary and secondary outcomes were changes in Montgomery-Asberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) scores assessed weekly and Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II) scores assessed daily during the 2-week stimulation phase. Exploratory outcomes included response and remission rates. Results: Of 57 randomized participants, 51 completed treatment (active, n=27; sham, n=24). The cohort exhibited moderate-to-severe treatment resistance (mean Maudsley Staging Method score, 10.9) and psychiatric comorbidity in 82% of participants. Active iTBS was associated with steeper MADRS improvement than sham (-3.54 points/week; 95% CI, -5.53 to -1.55; false discovery rate-adjusted P<.001), corresponding to model-estimated reductions of 12.06 versus 4.98 points (Cohen d=-0.89). BDI-II trajectories similarly favored active treatment, although with a smaller effect size (-0.23 points/day; 95% CI, -0.41 to -0.05; false discovery rate-adjusted P=.02; Cohen d=0.22). MADRS response rates were higher with active iTBS (42.3% vs 13.0%), whereas remission rates were numerically but not significantly greater (26.9% vs 12.5%). No serious adverse events occurred. Conclusions and Relevance: Accelerated connectivity-guided iTBS produced significant add-on antidepressant effects during acute inpatient treatment of TRD. Larger multicenter trials are needed to establish durability and optimize clinical implementation. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04832750 .

research.abstract: Multidrug efflux pumps are major drivers of antimicrobial resistance, but overlapping resistance mechanisms mask the physiological limits of efflux alone. Bacterial genomes encode a large repertoire of multidrug efflux pumps, which could theoretically combine to achieve exceptionally high levels of resistance. To delineate the extent of resistance achievable through efflux driven adaptation, we performed adaptive laboratory evolution of Mycobacterium smegmatis mc²155 wild-type and efflux-deleted (ΔlfrA, ΔefpA) strains against ethidium bromide, a broad-spectrum efflux substrate. Despite prolonged selection, resistance reproducibly plateaued at 8-16 fold increase in MIC under the tested conditions. This plateau emerged through distinct evolutionary trajectories characterized by non-overlapping efflux pump sets: from overexpression of the well-characterized lfrA to upregulation of multiple uncharacterized pumps, all conferring cross-resistance. Genetic reconstruction of mutations in a transcriptional regulator and a membrane protein, together with overexpression of efflux pumps, recapitulated the resistance phenotypes of the evolved strains. Sustained pump overexpression depleted membrane potential and drove metabolic suppression, suggesting that energetic exhaustion may constrain further increase in efflux-mediated resistance. Similar constraints were observed in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, indicating that they may extend to other mycobacterial species. Efflux-metabolic integration thus affects resistance evolution, revealing therapeutic vulnerabilities to combat multidrug resistance.

research.abstract: The Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC) is a genetically conserved group of pathogens whose lineage diversity has important biological, clinical, epidemiological, and public health implications. Human- and animal-adapted MTBC lineages differ in phylogeographic distribution, host association, transmission, drug resistance patterns, phenotypic traits, and diagnostic relevance. This narrative review summarizes the currently described MTBC lineages, including geographically restricted and recently recognized groups, and examines how lineage and sublineage structure can influence these characteristics. It also examines classical and genomic genotyping approaches, including IS 6110 -restriction fragment length polymorphism (RFLP), spoligotyping, mycobacterial interspersed repetitive unit-variable number tandem repeat (MIRU-VNTR), and SNP-based classification using whole-genome sequencing (WGS), with particular emphasis on lineage-dependent differences in discriminatory performance and phylogenetic resolution. Particular attention is given to lineage-associated variation in transmission, drug resistance, cell envelope composition, diagnostic interpretation, and genomic surveillance. This review also addresses inconsistencies between historical and genomic nomenclature. Integrating harmonized classification, broader genomic sampling, clinical, epidemiological, and phenotypic data will improve interpretation of MTBC diversity and its application to tuberculosis surveillance and control.

research.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) in Oman remains above the pre-elimination threshold of the End TB Strategy, largely due to cases among the expatriate population. Pyrazinamide (PZA), a key first-line anti-TB drug that shortens treatment duration, is increasingly threatened by rising PZA resistance (PZA-R). This study analyzed 241 Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) isolates collected across Oman between 2018 and 2023, including PZA-resistant (PZA-R) (n = 105) and PZA-susceptible (PZA-S) (n = 74) isolates. Drug susceptibility testing was performed using BD MGIT SIRE/PZA kits. Mutations in candidate PZA resistance genes (pncA, panD, and rpsA) and spoligotype profiles were assessed, while a subset of 96 isolates underwent whole-genome sequencing (WGS). MTB isolates showed high genetic diversity, comprising ten clades across four major lineages, with PZA-R predominating in lineage 1. Mutations in pncA, panD, and rpsA showed low sensitivity (≈10%) but high specificity (97.5%) for detecting PZA-R. Consistent with these findings, WGS showed poor concordance with phenotypic PZA resistance (κ = 0.15), but accurately predicted resistance to rifampicin (κ = 0.85) and isoniazid (κ = 0.79). Genome-wide association analysis identified 16 genes associated with PZA-R; however, the detected variants were not consistently linked to the resistant phenotype, suggesting lineage-specific polymorphisms or compensatory adaptations. Phylogenetic analysis revealed substantial diversity, with PZA-R isolates distributed across multiple lineages differing by more than 50 SNPs. These findings highlight substantial genotype-phenotype discordance in PZA resistance and support further studies integrating quantitative phenotyping and genomic analysis. Further genomic studies can therefore improve resistance prediction and monitoring of the spread of drug resistance.

research.abstract: Bacterial genomes encode a diverse array of proteins that function in a coordinated manner to orchestrate the highly dynamic process of cell division. Over the course of evolution, Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mt) and related mycobacterial species have diverged from the model bacterial species such as E. coli and B. subtilis and acquired distinct, poorly conserved proteins that underpin their distinct mechanisms of growth and division. However, the identity and functional roles of these molecular determinants remain largely elusive. In the present study, we identified two additional Di Viva domain-containing proteins of mycobacteria, Msm0050 and Msm5083, and performed detailed functional characterization of Msm5083/Rv1209, thereby expanding the known repertoire of DivIVA domain-containing proteins in this species. Although homologous to Wag31 and SepIVA (the known mycobacterial DivIVA domain-containing proteins), they show distinct cell division defects. Functional studies using an Msm5083 deletion mutant highlighted its role in lipid biosynthesis and maintaining cell envelope integrity, and hence, we named it CidIVA (cell envelope integrity determinant DivIVA). Subcellular localization and interactome analysis demonstrated that it homes to the membrane and interacts with other membrane-associated proteins involved in membrane synthesis and maintenance, lipid metabolism, and transportation, consistent with the observed phenotypes. Interestingly, Rv1209, the orthologue of Msm5083, showed enrichment at the poles and lateral cell wall and predominant interactions with virulence-related proteins. Although dispensable for in vitro survival , it is required for Mtb survival in vivo . Overall, our study identifies two novel DivIVA domain-containing proteins, one of which forms a functional nexus linking lipid homeostasis, cell-envelope maintenance and cell division. These results not only advance our understanding of mycobacterial cell biology but also suggest broader principles of functional diversification within multi-member protein families across bacterial species.

research.abstract: Abstract Retrospective reassessment of archival brain banks provides opportunities to identify previously undocumented neuropathologies. However, limited tissue availability and preservation, together with differences in sampling and staining protocols across brain banks, can con-strain the histological information available for analysis. This study investigated whether computational models can integrate complementary information across histological stains and retain discriminative information under incomplete stain availability. A deep learning model incorporating shared-specific feature modeling, cross-stain knowledge distillation, and random modality masking was developed and evaluated on 1, 607 whole slide images from the dorsolateral frontal cortex of 602 donors across three cohorts. Using chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) and Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and their comorbidity as a proof-of-principle application, our model achieved macro-averaged areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.899, 0.904, and 0.898 across three stain-defined groups, exceeding corresponding single-stain baselines. Discriminative performance was retained when each group’s defining stain was withheld. Model-predicted disease probabilities were associated with neuropathological staging measures for AD and CTE, and spatial attribution patterns on the remaining stains were largely preserved under defining-stain masking. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of leveraging complementary and partially overlapping histopathological information under incomplete stain availability, providing a foundation for future computational studies across brain regions and brain banks.

research.abstract: Abstract Relationships among the five subfamilies of Linnina within Dipsacales remain contentious. Extensive nuclear gene-tree discordance and cytonuclear discordance involving Linnaeoideae complicate reconstruction of their early evolutionary history. We analyzed whole-genome resequencing data from 88 Dipsacales species representing all nine subfamilies and eight outgroups. Using Dipsacales-specific nuclear reference locus sets, we recovered 3,023 orthologous nuclear loci. Nuclear analyses consistently placed (Morinoideae + Zabelioideae) sister to (Linnaeoideae + (Valerianoideae + Dipsacoideae)) across inference methods and character-coding schemes. Despite strong backbone support, extensive gene-tree discordance persisted at deep nodes. Node-level analyses suggested that incomplete lineage sorting (ILS) was a major source of discordance, while evidence for ancient gene flow varied among nodes. At the Linnaeoideae + (Valerianoideae + Dipsacoideae) node, topology frequencies approached ILS-only expectations, whereas internal branch lengths supported a model incorporating gene flow. At the Morinoideae + Zabelioideae node, multiple analyses provided more consistent evidence of ancient gene flow. ILS-only simulations recovered the observed plastid placement of Linnaeoideae in 8.63% of replicates, indicating that ILS could generate this topology; ancient gene flow, potentially involving plastid capture, remains a possible explanation for the cytonuclear discordance. Divergence-time estimates placed four major Linnina backbone divergences between 56.87 and 48.77 Ma. These findings suggest that early Linnina diversification involved successive lineage divergences and extensive ancestral polymorphism sorting, potentially accompanied by ancient gene exchange among some ancestral lineages. research.abstract: ABSTRACT Mycobacterium tuberculosis contains thirteen Mycobacterial membrane protein Large (MmpL) transporters, which belong to the family of secondary active RND transporters. MmpL4 and MmpL5, together with their operon partners MmpS4 and MmpS5, export the mycobacterial siderophore mycobactin and the last resort TB drug bedaquiline. Recently, we determined a structure of the MmpL4 monomer in complex with desferrated mycobactin, which lacked a functionally essential coiled-coil domain predicted to extend far into the periplasm. Here, we present a cryo-EM structure of the hexameric (MmpS4) 3 -(MmpL4) 3 complex, which was enabled by rational disulfide cross-links based on AlphaFold predictions. We observed density for the coiled-coil domain, which protrudes into the periplasmic space at an angle of around 60° relative to the symmetry axis of the MmpL4 trimer. In the context of the hexameric complex, MmpL4’s conformation differs strikingly from the one observed for monomeric MmpL4, which includes formation of a large cavity in the periplasmic domain and rearrangements of conserved proton coupling residues at the transmembrane domain. Two of the cross-linked variants were found to be functionally defective, indicating that the hexameric complex undergoes substantial conformational changes to accomplish mycobactin and drug transport.

research.abstract: SUMMARY Background Tuberculosis (TB) remains a leading infectious cause of death, with drug-resistant TB (DR-TB) challenging disease control. Brazil has a high TB burden, and Rio Grande do Sul state reports persistently high incidence and drug-resistance rates. The drivers shaping the regional DR-TB burden remain poorly characterised. Methods We conducted genomic surveillance of confirmed DR-TB cases in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, from January 2023 to September 2024. Clinical isolates underwent genotypic (gDST) and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing (pDST) and whole-genome sequencing (WGS). We analyzed 33 newly sequenced genomes and 267 historical Mycobacterium tuberculosis genomes collected in 2011–2019 to characterize resistance, transmission, and spatiotemporal patterns and estimate the contributions of transmitted and acquired rifampicin resistance. Findings Molecular testing detected rifampicin resistance missed by pDST, including borderline rpoB mutations in 18.2% and emerging resistance-associated variants in 3% of the 33 analyzed isolates. Conversely, pDST detected baseline bedaquiline resistance missed by WGS in one newly diagnosed case. Among 300 genomes, 181 (60.3%) clustered into 32 genomic clusters at a 5-SNP threshold, including 12 with long-term circulation and several spanning prisons and communities. Sublineage frequencies remained stable over time, whereas we observed marked geographic structuring and localized clonal expansion. Among 178 rifampicin-resistant isolates, transmission accounted for an estimated 79.2–88.2% of resistance, corresponding to 11.8–20.8% of cases arising through de novo acquisition during treatment. Interpretation Our findings identify active transmission as the main driver of rifampicin-resistant TB in Rio Grande do Sul, with long-term transmission chains extending across both incarcerated and community settings. These results underscore the urgent need to strengthen timely TB case detection and resistance testing, enhance contact investigations, and implement targeted interventions aiming to interrupt persistent transmission chains.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Tuberculosis remains a major public health challenge in Ghana, where GeneXpert MTB/RIF serves as a first–line diagnostic tool. However, uncertainties about this method persist regarding specimen quality and the clinical significance of indeterminate rifampicin susceptibility results. Methods We conducted a retrospective cross–sectional study of samples from 3,977 presumptive TB patients tested either at HopeXchange Medical Center (Kumasi) or Keta Municipal Hospital between January 2020 and December 2024. Demographic data, sputum macroscopic appearance, and GeneXpert results were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Fisher’s exact test. Results Overall Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTb) test positivity was 11.6% (461/3977). Males accounted for 63.3% of positive results, with the highest percentage among those ages 30–40 years. Mucopurulent specimens yielded the highest positivity rate (25.4%), compared to 4.0% of salivary specimens. Blood–stained sputum specimens (n=44) showed a 15.9% positivity rate. Although confirmed rifampicin resistance was low (1.7%), 9.3% of all MTb positive samples yielded an indeterminate result. The rate of indeterminate results from samples collected at Kwadaso Municipal increased from 7.3% in 2021 to 28.6% in 2024. research.abstract: Despite longstanding infant pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV13), residual vaccine-type (VT) carriage persists in Malawi, where human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) prevalence is high. Adults living with HIV (ALWH) on long-term (>1 year) antiretroviral therapy (ART) show higher pneumococcal carriage and shedding than HIV-uninfected adults, but their contribution to VT transmission remains unclear. We conducted a longitudinal household study in Malawi with weekly nasopharyngeal sampling and fitted a household transmission dynamic model using Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods. We collected 906 samples from 302 participants: younger children (0-5 years), older children (6-17 years) and adults (18+ years) stratified by HIV status and ART duration. VT transmission was more intense with household mixing, with ALWH on long-term ART contributing most to onward transmission to younger children. In contrast, non-vaccine serotype (NVT) transmission was driven mainly by younger children across multiple household pathways. Younger children and ALWH on long-term ART had prolonged carriage, which may have sustained household transmission. VT acquisition was driven mainly by household exposure, whereas NVT acquisition was balanced between household and community sources. Unvaccinated ALWH substantially contribute to household pneumococcal transmission, sustaining residual VT carriage. Optimal pneumococcal vaccination strategies targeting ALWH should be evaluated in high HIV prevalence low-income settings.

research.abstract: Computing phylogenetic likelihoods becomes challenging when the continuous-time Markov chain has a large state space. At each branch, pruning algorithms require terms of the form $e^{Q t}\cdot B$, where $Q$ is an $S \times S$ rate matrix (e.g., for $S$ states), $t$ is a branch length, and the columns of matrix $B$ (e.g., $B \in \mathbb{R}_{+}^{S \times L}$) are partial-likelihood vectors for $L$ site patterns. Many implementations calculate the dense transition matrix $P(t)=e^{Q t}$ via eigendecomposition and multiply it by $B$. This strategy is efficient for small state spaces, but it can be inefficient for large sparse rate matrices because forming $P(t)$ or its eigen vector matrices destroys sparsity and its cost may not be well amortized when $L$ is small. We implement an alternative likelihood kernel based on the Al-Mohy and Higham (2011) algorithm for computing the action of the matrix exponential directly, avoiding explicit construction of $P(t)$ or its eigen vector matrices. The resulting method takes full advantage of the sparsity of $Q$. We implement this method as a CPU-based extension to the BEAGLE library and evaluate it on two large-state molecular models: a Markov-modulated codon model of heterotachy with $M$ selective regimes and $61\cdot M$ possible states, and a codon-pair model of interlocus gene conversion between two paralogs with $61^2=3\,721$ possible states. Our results characterize when action-based likelihood computation improves performance over calculating $e^{Q t}$ directly. We show that this method enables fast, scalable inference for complex models, removing a key computational barrier to the study of evolution with large state space models.

research.abstract: Abstract Horizontal gene transfer mediated by conjugative plasmids is a primary driver of bacterial evolution and the spread of adaptive traits, including antibiotic resistance determinants. Tracking how these plasmids disseminate through complex microbial communities remains a major challenge. Current methodologies often yield static, endpoint snapshots of host identity, overlooking transient transfer events and plasmid encounters with the co-resident mobilome. To overcome these limitations, we introduce SPacer Integration (SPI) plasmids, which turn the mobile element itself into a recorder of its own transfer history. We engineered conjugative and mobilizable plasmids to carry a CRISPR-Cas adaptation cassette ( cas1–cas2 and a minimal CRISPR array) and maintain tight repression of cas1-cas2 expression in the donor cell, so that upon transfer they capture spacers from the chromosome and plasmids of new hosts and store them permanently in their own array. Subsequent PCR amplification and sequencing of these expanded arrays provide a molecular record of both the bacterial hosts and the co-resident plasmids encountered. We created SPI plasmids using the backbones of well-characterized mobilizable and conjugative plasmids RSF1010, RP4, F, and R100-1. We tested SPI plasmids in defined laboratory matings and in complex wastewater communities. The analysis of the acquired spacers successfully mapped permissive host ranges and profiled the co-resident plasmids in situ . Requiring only standard cloning, PCR and sequencing, this accessible and cost-effective strategy establishes a new framework for studying plasmid ecology. Because spacers are integrated chronologically, it further offers the potential to reconstruct multi-step transfer trajectories across natural microbial networks.

research.abstract: Abstract Integrating grazing animals into nut orchards can introduce foodborne pathogens including Salmonella enterica and Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC) into crop production environments. This study investigated pathogen transfer and persistence in the soil following livestock grazing (sheep/chicken) in two organic almond orchards and one walnut orchard in California. Soil and fecal samples were collected periodically for 120 days after grazing. Enrichment, selective culture and PCR were used for STEC and Salmonella enterica detection. Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) was assessed using microdilution assays, and whole genome sequencing (WGS) was used to characterize AMR genes, virulence genes and population structure. All 284 soil and 79 fecal samples collected tested negative for Salmonella enterica and E. coli O157. Presumptive STEC was detected by colony PCR in 3.2% (n = 9/284, 95% CI 1.7-5.9%) of the soil samples, and 34.2% (n = 27/79, 95% CI 24.7-45.2%) of fecal samples. Shiga toxin genes were confirmed by WGS in 15 of 31 sequenced isolates. Predominant subtypes were stx 1c and stx 2b , and O176:H4 and O174:H2 were the most common serotypes. Phenotypic AMR was detected in 33.3% (n = 12/36) of isolates, with multidrug resistance in 8.3% (n = 3/36). A soil and a sheep fecal isolate differed by one core-genome single nucleotide polymorphism and shared a closed multidrug-resistance plasmid of identical gene content, consistent with a lineage resident in the flock that transferred to soil. Confirmed STEC in orchard soil was rare and transient. These results provide evidence to inform food safety guidelines on crops integrated with livestock. Importance Farmers use grazing animals including chicken and sheep in nut orchards to improve the health of the soil and productivity of the orchard while also increasing sustainability. However, animals can shed bacteria that cause foodborne disease, and as nuts come into contact with the orchard soil before harvest, bacteria surviving in the orchard could contaminate the crop. Growers wait a fixed period between grazing and harvest, however bacterial survival may vary with climate, soil conditions and animal species. In this study, Shiga toxin-producing E. coli was common in sheep feces but was rarely confirmed in orchard soil, and most bacteria isolated from chicken feces did not carry Shiga toxin genes when their genomes were sequenced. The bacteria of greatest concern, Salmonella enterica and E. coli O157, were not found in any samples. This research can inform grazing guidance for nut orchards, supporting both food safety and sustainable farming.

research.abstract: Abstract Understanding genetic backgrounds and potential migration routes of emerging pathogens is important for preventing further invasions and outbreaks. RNA-seq data from field-collected infected plant tissues are increasingly used for pathogen monitoring, particularly for pathogens that cannot be cultured on artificial media. Despite its advantages, low pathogen read proportions in such field RNA-seq data can lead to unreliable genotyping results, hindering accurate surveillance and diagnosis. Plasmopara viticola , the causal agent of grapevine downy mildew, is one of the most destructive grapevine pathogens. Historical records and previous studies suggest that this pathogen originated in North America and has spread worldwide, including to Japan. However, the phylogenetic relationship between P. viticola populations in Japan and other geographic regions remains unknown, largely because culturing this obligate biotrophic pathogen is labor-intensive. Here, inspired by a peel technique used in paleobotany, we developed a new sampling method that effectively collects epiphytic P. viticola material using a cellulose acetate membrane filter. Samples collected using this method yielded higher RNA quantity and quality than conventional leaf discs. Moreover, the new method significantly enriched pathogen biomass relative to host tissues. By integrating newly obtained field RNA-seq data and publicly available whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data, we conducted single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) calling and phylogenetic analysis. Our results indicated that the Japanese samples tested are genetically distinct from isolates mainly collected in European countries. In conclusion, this new sampling technique simplifies field sample collection of this agriculturally important plant pathogen and provides insights into developing better-informed management strategies.

research.abstract: Estimating dengue force of infection (FOI) is essential for understanding transmission dynamics and targeting intervention programmes, yet surveillance data in endemic settings required for estimations are often incomplete, with varying formats. We developed a Bayesian hierarchical catalytic model that jointly fits age-stratified case data, aggregate case data, and seroprevalence surveys within a single framework, incorporating external covariates to improve parameter identifiability. Synthetic validation showed that covariates alone recovered accurate FOI point estimates even when most districts contributed only aggregate data, but did so with poorly calibrated uncertainty; anchoring the model with a single seroprevalence survey was necessary to bring credible interval coverage close to nominal. Applied to 128 districts across Java and Bali, Indonesia (2016-2024), the model revealed substantial spatial heterogeneity in FOI and reporting rates. Many districts in Java exceeded the WHO-suggested seroprevalence threshold for vaccine introduction, yet were classified as low-priority when using reported incidence as prioritisation criterion, particularly in areas with weak surveillance. Model-based seroprevalence estimation, integrating multiple data sources, offers a more consistent basis for identifying high-priority districts for vaccine introduction, and is less susceptible to surveillance bias than reported incidence.

research.abstract: Shingles (herpes zoster), caused by reactivation of varicella zoster virus (VZV), affects about one third of people during their lifetime, and host genetics contribute to susceptibility. We performed a genome-wide association study (GWAS) meta-analysis across five cohorts comprising 70,216 cases and 1,646,257 controls of European ancestry. We identified eight genome-wide significant loci, replicating associations in the HLA region and near IFNA21 and identifying novel associations near BACH2, IFNAR2, RHOBTB1, KPNB1 and CPN1 and at the IGH locus. HLA fine-mapping identified eight independent allele signals, six at HLA-B, with the strongest protective association for HLA-B*44:02/B*44:27. Colocalization linked the risk alleles to lower expression of IFNAR2 in T cells, NK cells and skin, BACH2 in CD4⁺ T cells, and IGHG1 and IGHG2 in B cells. These loci implicate MHC class I antigen presentation, type I interferon signaling, T-cell memory and humoral immunity. Shingles was genetically correlated with pain, infectious and immune-mediated diseases. In Mendelian randomization, genetic liability to shingles was associated with multiple sclerosis and systemic lupus erythematosus, but both associations depended on the MHC instrument, suggesting shared HLA effects. Genetic liability to pain was associated with higher shingles risk. These findings advance understanding of the genetic architecture of VZV reactivation.

research.abstract: Streptococcus pyogenes causes diseases ranging from mild pharyngitis to life-threatening invasive infection, yet the genomic determinants of this variation remain poorly understood. We analyzed 1,863 publicly available genomes, whose pangenome comprises 6,568 genes (1,392 core and soft-core, 656 shell, and 4,520 cloud), and grouped isolates into 15 genetic groups with FastBAPS. Ten groups were monophyletic on the global phylogeny, and non-monophyly of the remaining five largely reflected the placement of isolates from group 12, which is dispersed across the tree. A GenomegaMap scan identified 163 of 3,147 genes with {omega} > 1. These genes were depleted among core genes and enriched among cloud genes, a pattern consistent with positive selection on recently acquired genes but also with the retention of slightly deleterious variation in young genes. A putative IS transposase (K07497) was the most consistent functional enrichment signal, which led us to analyze insertion sequence (IS) elements directly. In group 12, complete IS copies within genomes were more often near-identical than in other groups (OR = 1.46), consistent with more recent IS activity, and genes with {omega} > 1 were 2.9 times more likely than other accessory genes to lie within 5 kb of an IS element (8.8% vs. 3.0%; permutation p = 0.0006) after excluding IS-encoded genes. We did not detect this association in any other group, and most genes under selection were not IS-proximal.
